title: Klaviyo Composer: Features, Limits and Cross-App Use
summary: Klaviyo Composer automates email tasks within the platform, removing the need for external tools. See what it does and how your workflow changes.
body_markdown:
## Measurable new features in Composer


Klaviyo states what Composer does but publishes no figures for it. What's measurably new comes down to a short list of described capabilities and nothing you can benchmark. That matters when you decide how much of your stack to rewire.


> What's measurably new comes down to a short list of described capabilities and nothing you can benchmark.


### Capabilities Klaviyo states


[Klaviyo's marketing agent blog post](https://www.klaviyo.com/blog/composer-marketing-agent) calls Composer "an AI marketing agent available to every Klaviyo customer that analyzes business data, identifies priorities, and completes marketing work." Each of those verbs stays inside Klaviyo's own data:


- It reads what's in your account
- It ranks what to do
- It does the work there


If a job starts in your helpdesk or ends in your ad platform, none of those verbs reaches it.


[Klaviyo's community post](https://community.klaviyo.com/product-updates-and-announcements-51/new-a-dedicated-space-for-all-things-composer-19874) describes Composer as a way to "explore new ways to create email and SMS campaigns with AI," and announces a dedicated community space for it.


Take the space as the place to read how other teams use it and to ask questions before you change a live flow. It's not documentation of limits.


### What the pages do not say


None of the three pages gives a number: no time saved, no lift in revenue, no count of supported actions. They also don't list triggers it can receive from outside Klaviyo, or fields it can write to other apps.


Without those, you can't yet say Composer replaces any cross-app step, so check the Composer page itself before you remove anything.
